To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) joint attention begins to develop in the first year of life; (b) it involves a whole-brained system that integrates triadic information about the self, the social partner, and a common referent; (c) it is neurodevelopmentally continuous with the functional development of the human social brain; (d) it contributes to the functional neurodevelopment of theory of mind; and (e) the neurodevelopment of this system is abnormal in autism.

the neurodevelopmental trajectory of joint attention contributes substantially to the development of the neural systems for human joint attention and social cognition, including theory of mind ability.
The development of joint attention is associated with the development of the human social brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the hypothesis that joint attention contributes to neurodevelopmental systems for social cognition in typical development and in ASD.
understanding how joint attention develops in typically developing (TD) children, and how it is neurodevelopmentally impaired in children with ASD.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
joint attention is a key component of the neurodevelopment of human social cognition.
joint attention is the most important social-cognitive neurobehavioral system in human social-cognitive neurobiology.
the neurodevelopmental trajectory of joint attention is an essential component of the neurodevelopment of social cognition in typically developing individuals and ASD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the neurodevelopmental continuity hypothesis of joint attention and theory of mind is supported by the new imaging literature.

(a) joint attention is neurodevelopmentally continuous with theory of mind and other social-cognitive abilities, (b) the neurodevelopment of theory of mind and related social-cognitive abilities is a major contributor to the neurodevelopment of the social brain, and (c) the social-cognitive neuroimaging literature on ASD is consistent with this model.
the neurodevelopmental continuity hypothesis of the social brain and social cognition is supported by the imaging literature on the development of joint attention.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neurodevelopmental study of joint attention provides an important and underutilized perspective on the neurodevelopmental basis of the social brain.

joint attention is an important and unique aspect of social cognition that can be studied with neuroimaging methods, and is an excellent candidate for future research on the neural mechanisms of social-cognitive development.
joint attention, as a whole-brain neurodevelopmental process, is a key component of the neurodevelopment of human social cognition.
